issues.legal_issue: An unexplained, substantial delay in filing a writ petition challenging a land acquisition is a sufficient ground to dismiss the petition.
material_facts: The petitioners challenged the validity of a land acquisition by filing a writ petition.
The acquisition notifications had been issued years before the petition was filed; the petition was filed more than 17 months after the award and after the Collector had taken possession.
The petitioners did not satisfactorily explain the delay.
issues.conclusion: The unexplained delay was a sufficient ground to dismiss the writ petition, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Whether delay warrants dismissal depends on the facts of each case. Unexplained delay in seeking writ relief may itself justify dismissal. The judgment notes that counsel referred to this Court's decisions on delay but does not identify them by name; it cites no statutory provision as the basis for this conclusion.

predicates.writ_challenges_land_acquisition: The petitioners filed a writ petition challenging the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.filing_was_substantially_delayed: The petitioners filed the writ petition substantially later than the acquisition notifications and more than 17 months after the award.
predicates.delay_lacked_explanation: The petitioners did not satisfactorily explain the delay in filing.

issues.definition: When a party substantially delays filing a writ petition challenging a land acquisition and does not explain the delay, the petition is dismissed for delay.
